title: Observer Orchestrator for Prompt Guardrails and Auto-Quarantine
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build an 'Observer Orchestrator' service that binds curated eval prompt sets to live rollout traffic and enforces adaptive quarantine policies. The orchestrator will run in the control plane and perform: 1) probabilistic sampling of canary/shadow requests mapped to golden prompt families, 2) multi-metric scoring (accuracy proxies, hallucination heuristics, latency regressions) against per-customer scorecards, 3) fuzzy drift detection to avoid noisy flips, and 4) automated quarantine + human-in-loop escalation for high-confidence regressions. This is intended to complement existing canary rollouts and A/B experiments by providing prompt-aware guardrails rather than coarse aggregate thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Observer orchestrator can subscribe to canary and shadow streams and sample requests according to policy (percent + seed).
Samples are mapped to named eval prompt families and evaluated using the eval-service score API within 1s of sampling for streaming workloads.
Multi-metric fusion produces a single regression score and a categorical action: ignore, warn, soft-quarantine, hard-quarantine.
Soft-quarantine reduces affected variant weight by a configurable percent and notifies rollout conductor; hard-quarantine automatically shifts traffic to fallback variant and creates incident ticket.
Human-in-loop review flow available in Console with diff view of golden-set vs live outputs and links to underlying prompts and model parameters.
End-to-end tests and a staging smoke harness that simulates subtle drift and clear regressions.
Metrics and dashboards surfaced in Console: per-prompt-family regression rate, quarantine actions, latency impact, and time-to-detect.
No customer data leaves the customer's region for private deployments (honor VPC/on-prem constraints).
implementation_notes: Leverage existing eval-service APIs; add mapping layer that groups live inputs to nearest golden family via fingerprint hashing.
Use a sliding-window bayesian filter to stabilize decisions and avoid flip-flops during transient noise.
Fusion model will be rule-based initially (weighted score of quality, hallucination, latency) with telemetry hooks for future ML-based calibrator.
Integrate with rollout-conductor to apply gradual soft-quarantine weights and to escalate to hard-quarantine when hysteresis threshold crossed.
Respect model variant compatibility: only compare outputs to golden prompts when model architecture and tokenization are compatible or use normalized-output layer.
Ensure sampling policy is configurable per-customer and per-project; defaults tuned to low overhead (0.5-2% of traffic).
risks_and_mitigations: False positives from noisy prompts -> mitigation: conservative hysteresis and require multi-metric agreement before quarantine.
Increased latency for sampled requests -> mitigation: asynchronous eval where possible and bounded evaluation timeout (200ms for sync path).
Privacy/regulatory exposure in Private deployments -> mitigation: orchestrator runs inside customer VPC or on-prem process and only stores hashes and metadata unless customer opt-in is enabled.
Operational complexity for small customers -> mitigation: sensible defaults and opt-out toggle via Console and API.
Rollout race conditions -> mitigation: centralized lease in rollout-conductor for making weight changes and audit log entries.
